provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Graduation gratitude
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state things they are grateful for
The pupils should be able to write a thank you prayer
Introduction:
We have learned about saying thank you.
Today we thank God for our school journey.
Content:
Gratitude means being thankful.
Think of your best day in school.
Think of your best friend in school.
Thank God for your teachers.
Thank God for your books.
Thank God for your water bottle.
Class activity:
Make a gratitude journal.
Draw pictures of things you thank God for.
Evaluation questions:
What is gratitude?
Name one thing you thank God for.
Why do we say thank you?
Summary:
We must always be grateful for our blessings.

topics.title: Blessing my school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to keep school clean
The pupils should be able to identify school property
Introduction:
Our school is our second home.
We must keep it clean and beautiful.
Content:
Do not litter the classroom.
Do not write on desks and walls.
Use the bin for rubbish.
Water the school plants.
Pick up papers on the ground.
Class activity:
Campus beautify duty.
Clean the classroom together.
Water the plants in the school garden.
Evaluation questions:
How do we keep our school clean?
Why should we not write on walls?
What is rubbish?
Summary:
We all have a duty to keep our school clean.

topics.title: Mentoring juniors
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to help younger pupils
The pupils should be able to list kind things to do for nursery one
Introduction:
We are big children now.
We must help the small children.
Content:
Show nursery one how to line up.
Teach them how to clean their hands.
Read a story to them.
Help them find their classroom.
Be kind to them when they cry.
Class activity:
Buddy hour.
Pair up with nursery one pupils.
Teach them how to draw a circle.
Evaluation questions:
How can we help nursery one pupils?
Why is it good to be kind to small children?
What should you do if a nursery one pupil cries?
Summary:
We are leaders and must help younger children.

topics.title: My next chapter
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state goals for primary one
The pupils should be able to write a simple goal letter
Introduction:
Next year we will go to primary one.
We must prepare for big school.
Content:
Goal means something you want to do.
I will read in primary one.
I will make new friends.
I will listen to my new teacher.
I will do my homework.
Class activity:
Write my goals letter.
Draw a picture of yourself in primary one.
Write one thing you will do in primary one.
Evaluation questions:
What is a goal?
Name one goal for primary one.
Why is it good to have goals?
Summary:
Goals help us prepare for the future.

topics.title: Courage for change
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what courage means
The pupils should be able to demonstrate brave behavior
Introduction:
Change can make us feel scared.
Courage helps us face change.
Content:
Courage is being brave.
Moving to primary one is change.
Making new friends is change.
Trying new food is change.
Standing up for others is courage.
Class activity:
Brave talk.
Stand up and say one brave thing you will do in primary one.
Practice speaking loudly and clearly.
Evaluation questions:
What is courage?
Name one change that needs courage.
How can you be brave at school?
Summary:
Courage helps us face new things without fear.

topics.title: Keeping the values
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list school values
The pupils should be able to explain why values are important
Introduction:
We have learned many values in school.
These values will help us in primary one.
Content:
Values are good behaviors.
Honesty is telling the truth.
Kindness is helping others.
Respect is listening to elders.
Sharing is giving to others.
Class activity:
Values passport.
Draw your favorite value in a small book.
Share with friends why you like that value.
Evaluation questions:
What are values?
Name one value you like.
Why do we need values?
Summary:
Good values help us everywhere we go.

topics.title: Blessing my parents
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state ways to honor parents
The pupils should be able to write a thank you letter
Introduction:
Our parents love us very much.
We must thank them for everything.
Content:
Honor means to show respect.
Listen to your parents.
Obey your parents.
Say thank you for gifts.
Help with small chores at home.
Pray for your parents.
Class activity:
Thank you letters.
Write a letter to mummy or daddy.
Draw a picture of your family.
Evaluation questions:
How do we honor our parents?
Why should we thank our parents?
Name one thing your parents do for you.
Summary:
We must always love and honor our parents.

topics.title: Prayer and blessing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say a prayer for their future
The pupils should be able to participate in group prayer
Introduction:
God loves us and hears our prayers.
We can pray for our future in primary one.
Content:
Prayer is talking to God.
Thank God for your teachers.
Ask God to help you learn.
Ask God to give you new friends.
Ask God to keep you safe.
Class activity:
Blessing circle.
Hold hands in a circle.
Each child says one prayer request.
Teacher prays for all children.
Evaluation questions:
What is prayer?
Why do we pray to God?
What can you pray for?
Summary:
God hears our prayers and blesses us.

topics.title: Legacy project final
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their legacy gift
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of legacy
Introduction:
A legacy is something we leave behind.
We will make a gift for our school.
Content:
Our legacy gift is beautiful drawings.
We draw things we love about school.
We draw our teachers and friends.
We write thank you notes.
We put them in a special book.
Class activity:
Finish our legacy gift.
 Color the last page of our legacy book.
 Write a message to the head teacher.
Evaluation questions:
What is a legacy?
Why do we make a legacy gift?
What will you put in your legacy book?
Summary:
Our legacy gift shows our love for our school.

topics.title: Graduation character send off
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify good character traits
The pupils should be able to give character awards
Introduction:
Today we celebrate our graduation.
We have learned about good character.
Content:
Good character means doing right.
We are kind to others.
We share our toys and books.
We listen to our teachers.
 We help friends who are sad.
Class activity:
Character awards and blessings.
 Give awards to friends for good character.
 Say a blessing to each child.
 Wear graduation caps and smile.
Evaluation questions:
What is good character?
Name one character trait you like.
Why is character important?
Summary:
Good character helps us succeed in life.
